amy_support: Hey @zoe_customer — I see you filed a ticket about a sudden invoice jump. Can you share a minimal repro and the SDK/runtime versions?
zoe_customer: Yep. Saw a ~2.5x jump this morning after switching to streaming + function calls. Local JS SDK estimator reports ~425 tokens but invoice shows ~1,100 tokens. Using redwood-js@2.3.1.
amy_support: Thanks. Can you paste (sanitized) request body or a curl so we can reproduce? Also include whether you used streaming stop/resume.
zoe_customer: Here is sanitized curl we ran (removed key):
```
curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat.stream \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-base-2","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the transcript"}],"functions":[{"name":"summarize","parameters":{}}],"stream":true}'
```
We also call the function tool and return structured JSON. No other middleware.
liam_eng: I'm looking at the payload — two areas to check: 1) server-injected system/tool preambles that we add for safety/function wrappers, and 2) how the client estimator handles streaming finalizations (stop event + buffered function output). Both can add a lot of tokens.
mike_devex: Also worth noting: the JS SDK estimator in 2.3.x uses a simplified tokenizer for streaming (fast byte-based estimate) while the billing pipeline uses the model's full tokenizer at service-side. That explains undercounts on some workloads. Function outputs that serialize large JSON (and KV caches we sometimes prepend) can cause completion token spikes.
billing-bot: Created escalation ticket BILL-987 and attached initial invoice lines for the customer id.
amy_support: Could you run the same request with stream=false and attach the server debug tokenization output? If you can't share full text, a redacted min repro is fine.
zoe_customer: Ran non-streaming repro. Local estimator: prompt=195, completion=230, total=425. Server debug (redacted) shows prompt=220, server_preamble=674, completion=206, total=1100. Uploaded gist: https://gist.github.com/redacted/min-repro.
liam_eng: That server_preamble number is key — we add an internal safety/tool wrapper and function-call scaffolding that isn't returned to the client but is counted by metering. It's expected in some cases but we should surface it so SDKs can estimate parity.
mike_devex: Quick practical steps: 1) Upgrade to redwood-js@2.4.0 — it includes a tokenizer upgrade and streaming finalization fixes. 2) Run our local token counter: `npx rw-token-count --model=rw-base-2 payload.json` (this uses the same tokenizer as billing). 3) If you need immediate credits, reply and we'll fast-path a billing review.
amy_support: For engineering: can we add an opt-in debug flag that returns server_injected_token_count in debug responses so clients can reconcile without sharing internal text?
liam_eng: Good idea. I've filed ENG-5544 to add a lightweight header `X-Redwood-Debug-Tokens: true` that will return counts only. Will include a note about function-call scaffolding and KV cache items.
zoe_customer: After upgrading to 2.4.0 and running npx rw-token-count my payload matches server counts within ~5 tokens. Thanks.
amy_support: Closing loop — escalated to billing for review of the invoice lines and flagged for adjustment if needed. Follow-up: ENG-5544 plus docs update in SDK guide about estimator parity. :thumbsup:
mike_devex: TL;DR for other customers: if you see big deltas, check for server-injected preambles and use `npx rw-token-count` or upgrade SDK to 2.4.x for parity.
billing-bot: Billing note: pending manual review under BILL-987.
amy_support: Marking thread as escalated -> eng + billing. Will update when billing completes the audit.
